html:
SMTO-CTX-0032 — SMTO can't find a saved result for that reference

GUID: d9f2e6fc-aec4-5cec-876b-52acc4ceafd5
Slug: result-unavailable
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: stored-result-recovery

What happened

  • The task asked for a saved result using a name that doesn't match any result it is allowed to see. It may be from another task, already removed, or simply mistyped. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task continue. SMTO tells it to list this task's finished steps to find the right result. The list shows only results this task can use, each with its correct name.
  2. If you asked the task to use a result from a different task or conversation, select Steer and describe what you need from it in words instead. A task can only open saved results that belong to its own work.
  3. If the task keeps repeating the same lookup, select Stop current task and start a new task describing the result you need. Repeating a lookup that already failed will not find anything new.

What success looks like

  • The task finds and reads a saved result, or continues its work without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to rerun the original command just to get its output back; that could repeat changes it made.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The receipt resolver found no accessible stored execution receipt for the reference; it returns the same response for missing, deleted, out-of-scope or restricted receipts and does not reveal which applies.

What this means

  • The receipt resolver deliberately uses the same response for missing data, invalid ownership, deleted source state, restricted content and scope or grant mismatches. It cannot disclose whether an inaccessible receipt exists. Listing the task's operations or following an advertised continuation can supply a valid reference.

Why this can happen

  • The receipt resolver deliberately uses the same response for missing data, invalid ownership, deleted source state, restricted content and scope or grant mismatches. It cannot disclose whether an inaccessible receipt exists. Listing the task's operations or following an advertised continuation can supply a valid reference.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the reference against task_context.list for work/operations without guessing foreign task IDs.

How to fix it

  • Follow the returned next_action (task_context.list on work/operations) or an advertised continuation to obtain a valid receipt reference for this run, then read that. Do not repeat the same lookup unchanged, guess a _result ID, or rerun the original command to regenerate output.
  • Follow an advertised continuation or list this task's operations to find an accessible recorded result.

Retry and execution caution

  • Read again only after obtaining a valid accessible reference or an authorized state change.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized operation or advertised continuation provides a readable stored receipt.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat the same unavailable lookup unchanged or rerun the command merely to recover output.

Technical notes

  • The lookup executes no command and reveals no inaccessible receipt content.
  • The response does not distinguish absence from denied access or establish prior execution outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
